us.conditions: US citizens can enter Slovenia visa-free for tourism or business for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.

de.conditions: EU citizens have the right to free movement and can enter Slovenia with a valid national ID card or passport.

gb.conditions: British passport holders can travel visa-free in Slovenia and the Schengen area for up to 90 days in any 180-day window.

ru.conditions: Гражданам РФ для въезда в Словению требуется действующая шенгенская виза категории C.

dos.title: Buy an e-Vignette before driving on motorways
dos.description: Driving on Slovenian highways without a valid electronic vignette (e-vinjeta) results in heavy automated fines.

dos.title: Respect pristine nature and national parks
dos.description: Slovenia is fiercely eco-conscious; littering or wild camping in Triglav National Park is strictly prohibited.

dos.title: Drink the tap water
dos.description: Tap water is of supreme Alpine purity across all of Slovenia; drinking fountains are abundant in Ljubljana.

donts.title: Don't swim in Lake Bled from non-designated zones
donts.description: Swimming is regulated around the island; only swim in designated lido areas to preserve the ecosystem.

donts.title: Don't drive without headlights in daytime
donts.description: Daytime running lights or dipped headlights are mandatory at all times on all roads in Slovenia.

etiquette.tipping: Tipping is not compulsory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% in sit-down restaurants for good service is customary.
